d1_objective: The learner moves the sampling lattice across an occupied band, sees an in-band alias candidate enter or leave while both continuous candidates retain identical sample dots, finds the first phase-safe rate with a practical guard, and constructs the Nyquist-phase counterexample that defeats equality.

implementation_contract.export: default function AliasThresholdLab() with no required props
implementation_contract.client_boundary: Put use client before imports. Store only sample rate and edge-tone phase with useState; keep deterministic signal math and SVG geometry in the same module, with no effects or browser APIs.
implementation_contract.lazy_loading: Add only the explicit registry import promise. DemoHost already creates React.lazy components at module scope and owns Suspense; do not add next/dynamic, ssr:false, another Suspense layer, or a variable import path.
implementation_contract.kit: Panel outer container; two labelled PresetGroups; two Sliders; one TargetList; one Readout. No UI primitive changes are required.
implementation_contract.styling: Existing Tailwind theme classes and currentColor for axes/text; house amber #e2903a and blue #4c8dd6 plus solid/dashed and filled/hollow cues. No chart package, stylesheet, global CSS, or hard-coded light background.

signal_and_math.declared_band: Real continuous-time input is known a priori to be bandlimited to |f|<=B, B=4.0 kHz. This prior is essential: samples alone never exclude higher-frequency aliases.
signal_and_math.supplied_mixture: x(t)=cos(2pi*0.7k*t+20deg)+0.75cos(2pi*1.8k*t-35deg)+0.50cos(2pi*3.1k*t+45deg)+0.35cos(2pi*4.0k*t+phi). Frequencies are kHz, t is ms, and phi is the live edge-tone phase.
signal_and_math.universal_test_bank: Test each frequency separately at phases 0, 45, and 90 degrees. Per-tone normalization prevents the 0.35 edge component from being hidden by larger lower-frequency components.
signal_and_math.sampling: T_s=1/f_s ms and x[n]=x(n/f_s). The sample-rate control uses 6.00<=f_s<=10.00 kHz on a 0.25 kHz grid.
signal_and_math.alias_map: For a tone f, choose signed residue q=f-round(f/f_s)f_s in [-f_s/2,f_s/2], apparent frequency f_a=|q|, and apparent phase phi_a=phi when q>=0 and -phi when q<0.
signal_and_math.sample_equivalent_pair: For the 4 kHz edge tone and f_s>=4 kHz, x_A(t)=cos(2pi*4t+phi) and x_B(t)=cos(2pi*(f_s-4)t-phi). At t=n/f_s, x_B=cos(2pi*n-2pi*4n/f_s-phi)=x_A for every integer n. Candidate B is admissible only when f_s-4<=B; otherwise the declared bandlimit excludes it.
signal_and_math.ideal_reconstruction_model: For f<f_s/2, ideal bandlimited reconstruction returns the original tone. For f>f_s/2 it returns the mapped baseband alias. At f=f_s/2, the samples are (-1)^n cos(phi), so the sine quadrature is unobservable; the canonical sample-only reconstruction is cos(phi)cos(2pi*f*t). This is an ideal identifiability test, not a finite-filter simulation.
signal_and_math.error_metric: For each test tone, compute E=||x_hat-x||_2/max(||x||_2,Number.EPSILON) on M=512 deterministic times t_m=20m/M ms, then E_dB=20log10(E). Display exact-zero results at a -120 dB floor only; compare the unfloored E against 10^-3, equivalent to strictly below -60 dB.
signal_and_math.guard: Required Nyquist clearance is G=f_s/2-B>=0.50 kHz. This reserves a 0.50 kHz analog transition interval between the occupied edge and Nyquist; it is separate from the ideal reconstruction-error test.
signal_and_math.pass_rule: PASS iff every frequency/phase case has E<10^-3, every supplied tone is strictly below f_s/2, and G>=0.50 kHz. On the 0.25 kHz rate grid the unique lowest passing setting is f_s=9.00 kHz.
signal_and_math.equality_falsification: At f_s=8.00 kHz and phi=90 degrees, x_A and x_B are opposite nonzero 4 kHz sinusoids between sample instants, yet both sample to zero. Mark FALSIFIED when the equality rate is selected, sample-pair maximum mismatch is below 1e-12, and their continuous normalized separation exceeds 10^-3. Equality is therefore not a phase-independent reconstruction guarantee.
scope_guards: The -60 dB score is deterministic numerical evidence for the supplied finite test bank, while the replica/nonoverlap argument supplies the theorem-level condition.
The guard represents room for an analog anti-alias transition and does not claim a realizable filter has been designed.
No digital filter is offered after an in-band collision because identical samples contain no label identifying which analog candidate generated them.

controls: Rate PresetGroup plus sample-rate Slider min 6, max 10, step 0.25 kHz; preset highlight clears after an unmatched rate.
Boundary-phase PresetGroup plus edge-phase Slider min 0, max 90, step 1 degree; preset highlight clears after an unmatched phase.
guided_task: Raise or lower f_s and find the smallest setting for which the per-tone -60 dB suite and the 0.50 kHz guard both pass; TargetList recognizes 9.00 kHz.
Select Nyquist 8.00 and Sine null 90deg. Confirm that both continuous candidates hit the same all-zero dots while separating between samples; TargetList and Readout report FALSIFIED.

Return to Guard pass 9.00. Candidate B moves to 5.00 kHz, outside the declared 0-4 kHz input band; the visual names the bandlimit and analog anti-alias assumption that makes reconstruction defensible.
state_and_interaction.feedback_budget: At most 12 test cases times 512 points plus two short SVG curves are recomputed synchronously per input, comfortably below 200 ms without memoization, effects, workers, FFTs, or network access.

targets: Lowest guarded rate: current worst E_dB, Nyquist clearance, and required f_s=9.00 kHz.
Break equality with phase: maximum sample mismatch and between-sample normalized separation.
readout_fields: f_s, f_s/2, B=4.00 kHz, and clearance G
worst per-tone reconstruction error in dB and the frequency/phase case producing it
edge candidate f_B=f_s-4, whether it lies inside the declared band, sample mismatch, PASS/FALSIFIED/Not yet status
explicit message that post-sampling digital filtering cannot choose between identical records
readouts_and_visual.frequency_chart: Responsive SVG spectral lane with labelled 0, B=4 kHz, f_s/2, B+0.5 kHz required clearance, and the adjacent-replica edge f_s-B. Use overlap/touch/guard-pass text and hatched or outlined regions rather than color alone.
readouts_and_visual.waveform_chart: Responsive SVG over 0-1 ms showing solid x_A, dashed x_B, and one shared set of filled sample dots. Label both analog frequencies/phases directly. At 8 kHz/90deg the curves are opposite and all dots lie at zero; at 9 kHz the dashed 5 kHz candidate remains sample-equivalent but is marked outside the admitted band.
readouts_and_visual.mobile: Controls and charts stack at 360 px; preset buttons wrap; both SVGs use fluid width and mobile-safe viewBoxes with at least 12-unit labels and no horizontal scroll.
readouts_and_visual.theme_and_non_color: Axes/text use currentColor and opacity; source/candidate use solid versus dashed strokes and direct labels; pass/fail appears as text and TargetList marks as well as color. Verify light and dark.

accessibility.keyboard_touch: PresetGroup supplies native >=44 px buttons and Slider supplies native 44 px range inputs. Tab, Enter/Space, and arrow keys complete both tasks; no drag-only or pointer-only action.
accessibility.aria: Wrap each preset group in a named role=group; give sliders aria-valuetext with kHz/degrees. TargetList and Readout announce live results politely. Each SVG has role=img and a dynamic aria-label naming rates, candidate frequencies, sample equality, guard, error, and status.
accessibility.motion: No animation or timer; geometry updates immediately, so reduced-motion users lose no information.
accessibility.contrast: All conclusions have numeric/text and line-style cues; amber/blue never carry meaning alone.

deterministic_checks: For every integer n and all allowed f_s and phi, the edge pair samples agree algebraically; numerical maximum mismatch over the displayed samples must stay below 1e-12.
At f_s=8.00 kHz and phi=90deg, all edge samples have magnitude below 1e-12, x_A and x_B are opposite, their normalized separation is 2, and 20log10(2)=6.020599913279624 dB; falsification is true.

At f_s=8.00 kHz and phi=0deg, the two equality candidates coincide and the current boundary error floors at -120 dB, but the universal bank's 90deg case is 0 dB, so equality still fails the phase-safe suite.
At f_s=7.50 kHz the 4.0 kHz edge maps to 3.5 kHz with negated phase; on the 20 ms grid the equal-energy integer-cycle tones are orthogonal, giving E=sqrt(2) and 3.010299956639812 dB for phi=90deg.
At f_s=8.25 kHz every supplied tone is strictly below Nyquist and the ideal test error floors at -120 dB, but G=0.125 kHz, so pass is false.
At f_s=8.50 kHz the ideal test still passes but G=0.25 kHz, so the No guard preset fails.
At f_s=9.00 kHz, f_s/2=4.50 kHz, G=0.50 kHz, the edge image is 5.00 kHz outside the declared band, all ideal test errors are zero before display flooring, and PASS is true.
At f_s=8.75 kHz, G=0.375 kHz and pass is false; therefore 9.00 kHz is the lowest passing value on the exact 0.25 kHz grid.
Threshold comparisons are E<1e-3 and G>=0.50; exactly -60 dB fails, exactly 0.50 kHz clearance passes, and f=f_s/2 always fails the strict interior test.
Every slider endpoint produces finite frequencies, phases, samples, errors, and SVG coordinates. Exact zero uses a display floor only and never log10(0) in status logic.
